bullets.text: Combined ratio was just under 91 with an aggregate underwriting margin over nine points. All business components contributed well and met targets without subsidization, and Commercial Auto maintained healthy margins.
Q1 premium growth was 7%, the best rate achieved over the last 19 quarters; Commercial Auto remains down on volume, though showing continued signs of a slow recovery.

Performance suggests the multi-year goal to increase auto average policy life by a specified fixed annual amount remains very attainable through specific retention efforts and customer mix changes; customer leverage is very meaningful.

New application growth was strong across all lines. Late-2009 Agency auto production momentum carried into 2010; Direct auto growth remained strong, particularly in Internet sales, and special lines had a good seasonal start.

State results were acceptably balanced; much expected improvement from actions in watch-list personal injury protection states materialized. Florida, the largest premium state, operates outside targets on most products until actions take further hold.

Expense ratio of 21.7 remained stubbornly high during low-to-negative average premium changes, with advertising contributing to increased expenses; policies-in-force per FTE improved 12% versus a year ago, continuing significant two-year gains.

Total return on investments was 3.2% fully taxable equivalent; unrealized gains totaled $964M; debt-to-total capital ratio ended at 26%; completed sale of Professional Liability Group to ABA partner affiliate.
